page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes a bundled local storage capacity of 7559 GB and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 145,373.21 and a PassMark CPU score of 128,741.43. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), contribute to top-tier results in extended instructions and encryption. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 10,709.34 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 657.87 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier at 2,284.09.

This server is designed for highly parallelized, compute-heavy workloads that require substantial local storage but do not demand high memory-to-CPU ratios. Excellent multi-threaded decompression and database operations make it suitable for large-scale data processing, static web serving, and Redis deployments, where it achieves 196.23 million SET operations per second. It also supports CPU-based machine learning tasks, demonstrating strong prompt processing speeds of 223.28 tokens/sec for medium 7B LLM models. The low memory-per-core ratio offers a cost-efficient hardware profile for compute-bound tasks, avoiding the premium associated with memory-optimized instances.
description: The Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it includes 256.0 GB of RAM and a substantial 7559 GB of bundled local storage. While it lacks GPU acceleration, its hardware profile delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and exceptional memory bandwidth, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 145,373.21 and uncached read speeds of 657.87 GB/sec. Advanced vector and matrix extensions further accelerate cryptographic and mathematical operations. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for compute-intensive, storage-heavy workloads such as high-throughput database operations, Redis caching, multi-threaded data decompression, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
